body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. During procedural repairs use rules-greg-common-sense-2026-10-30. Repository instructions and the executor's actual direct permissions govern required validation and landing.

1. CODER owns changes, focused/new tests and the required independent review pair. Include affected dependency/boundary guards. Reviewers follow repository startup/recovery once per context. Each review attempt needs its original complete structured result and finding dispositions; missing required review evidence is not clean. Read retained results as an eligible root of the original project with delegationId + submissionAttempt + resultId, pinned across output pages.
2. CODER→MERGER: ONE complete READY names scope/item, Git base/tree, launcher-consistent state, review results/dispositions and run results/counts/fingerprint checks. Read full required results at their native references. No partial-package progress to Merger, duplicate exports or manual hash manifests for already identified records; transfer only an actually inaccessible required result once. Repairing delivery alone needs no new review/test.
3. MERGER is non-authoring: integrate onto current master, avoid already-landed changes, and assess dependencies/conflicts. Adopt a Coder's review only with the repository's unchanged-contribution proof and clean-carry conditions. Master movement alone needs no extra Merger pair. Conflicts, changed package content or unproved carry return to the Coder. A carried review never carries a gate or acceptance verdict.
4. Validate the exact final input through the standard launcher and current repository requirements. Reuse only an applicable complete PASS on identical final input; preserve the native exit, terminal outcome and automatic input check. A failed/unrun check is not a pass: diagnose and return actual defects to their owner. Read only bounded failure diagnostics; recover an existing result rather than rerun for delivery. Follow rules-greg-git-identity-2026-10-29 and rules-greg-equivalent-gate-hosts-2026-10-28; separate facts from unproved cause.
5. Land under existing standing approval or actual acting-session permission; no repeated routine go or extra approval round. For broken evaluation/observation/credit, use the ONE current temporary procedure above. Keep missing evidence/evaluation explicit and delivered items pending until genuine native completion; never fabricate a result, weaken a binding or edit policy/store to obtain done. Follow rules-commit-messages.
6. Use supported claims/handoffs and durable result wakes. Never impersonate, change clocks or bypass a foreign live claim. Before queue handoff verify the recipient's actual live project, workdir and tracker binding; rediscover recreated sessions. During another gate's unchanged input, respect its claim/root and resource limits. Before state reports recover available mail and terminal evidence; otherwise name the last observation/time. TermAl owns runs/logs/wakes, not an agent reading stdout. A send receipt records dispatch AT SEND TIME, never current wake/failure. For an actual suspected gap use the existing exact-message read and TARGET acknowledgement cursor; no polling or resend from an old receipt alone. ACK records processing, not comprehension or a guaranteed wake.
7. After merge AND closure, automatically remove the worktree/build output under rules-post-completion-cleanup. Retain only for a recorded active need with owner/end condition. No additional landing gate.

Each canonical rule has one editor; Merger2 edits TermAl merger-operating-procedure. Send corrections to its editor, replace stale current wording and full-read verify; history stays in task notes. Reconcile available withdrawals before publication. Distinguish local full reads from quoted cross-project reads; an unavailable project memory is an access gap.

MERGER→ARCHITECT3: only concrete collaboration failures needing a rule/workflow correction, with evidence, impact and owner. Routine runs, READY, queue, landing and repair progress stay with the task/coordinator. Architect3 is never a routine notify target/result relay/recovery owner. Architects correct rules and inform affected agents; no compliance-status loop. Coordinators relay through Advisor; Advisor never executes.

Batching direction preserved from Greg via Advisor#1743,2026-10-18T21:20Z: "Merger should batch 2–3 independent ready changes per integration instead of serial single-item landings. Select disjoint paths/no ordering dependency, carry each onto the same current master, resolve any actual conflict, then run one gate/review on the exact combined freeze. Keep conflicting/dependent changes separate. Make batch fan-in the default at next boundary." Merger remains non-authoring: Greg via Advisor#1745 (2026-10-19) said "Merger MUST NOT code product/test fixes." Current repository carry/review/gate rules still govern; old batch identities and assignments are spent.
